components.title: Sterling workbench
components.description: The Sterling workbench image that a hosted site runs for each person.

control-implementations.description: What the Sterling workbench's unit tests, in the workbench package's report, show about its hosted session.

implemented-requirements.description: Secrets an extension saves go to the person's own OpenBao path, never to memory.

statements.description: In a hosted session the workbench rebinds Theia's key store, through which its extensions keep their secrets, to a store that writes, reads, lists and deletes them under the person's own OpenBao KV path (kv/data/users/<entity id>/<service>/<account>) with the session's own OpenBao token. With no active session every call is refused and OpenBao is not called, and an OpenBao refusal or silence becomes a plain sentence that holds no secret, token or entity id. On a single computer the store is the system keyring; when the keyring cannot load, saving fails, and Theia's in-memory store is never used.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the site's OpenBao with the per-person KV policy and decides which secrets people may keep there.

implemented-requirements.description: The person's long-term keys stay in OpenBao.

statements.description: The workbench's key service signs with the person's long-term key only through OpenBao Transit: it logs in to OpenBao's step-up role with the forwarded sign-in token, signs with that token and then revokes it, and keeps no step-up token between signatures. It refuses without any OpenBao call when the token's acr is not the site's step-up value or its auth_time is missing, older than the step-up window or in the future. OpenBao makes and unwraps the person's data keys with their own key-encryption key, using the session token. In local mode none of these long-term keys is available.
statements.remarks: Your organization enrols each person's keys in the site's OpenBao and sets the step-up window.

implemented-requirements.description: A session acts only for the person it was started for.

statements.description: In a hosted session the workbench backend logs in to OpenBao with the forwarded sign-in token only when the token's email, the forwarded email header and the person the session was started for agree, ignoring case; on any disagreement it makes no login and shows that the sign-in check failed. Once active, a token or email header naming someone else is ignored. It renews its OpenBao token at half of each lease, revokes the token when the session stops, and puts no token or entity id in its status or its log lines.
statements.remarks: Your organization's Keycloak signs the person in; Theia Cloud starts one session per person.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench backend reaches only the addresses your organization configured.

statements.description: A request the workbench backend makes on behalf of its browser page, through Theia's backend request facade, may reach only the addresses your organization configured: the Open VSX address and the hosts of the model servers, as exact scheme, host and port patterns with no wildcard. With neither set the allow list is empty. Plain http is accepted only to a loopback model server, and a model server setting that is not a JSON list of addresses is refused with a sentence naming the setting.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the site's model servers and Open VSX address, and the site network policy limits egress for every pod.

implemented-requirements.description: Session pods run Node with the FIPS provider on a FIPS host.

statements.description: On the running site, the signed evidence export samples session pods and counts those where Node reports its FIPS provider on; the deployment collector passes only when every sampled session reports it. The OpenSSL FIPS provider of the RHEL 9 base is the module of CMVP certificate #5573, recorded with its approved-mode caveat in the dated hosted verification records.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the site's nodes in FIPS mode and produces the evidence export at least weekly.
